rubrics.justification: Describes an expanded blastocyst with thinned zona, identifiable compact ICM, and cohesive TE consistent with 3AA; slight overreach in mentioning possible early hatching/partial collapse from a single still image.
Thoroughly integrates age, tubal factor, ovarian reserve, semen parameters, endometrium, BMI, lifestyle, and first-cycle status with embryo prognosis, including the hydrosalpinx caveat.

Overall logic is clear and internally consistent, with probability estimates reasonably tied to embryo quality and patient factors; minor issue is some speculative discussion around very high AMH and endometriosis/polycystic implications.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based and aligned with IVF practice, especially SET in a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst and attention to hydrosalpinx; slight deviation is implying PGT-A after repeated failures in a 26-year-old without stronger indication.

Provides clear next steps for current transfer and contingency planning, including SET, hydrosalpinx assessment, luteal support, alcohol cessation, prenatal vitamins, and future uterine/embryology review if unsuccessful.
